newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE ITALIAN FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE ITALIAN FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Italian Serie A matches due to be
played on Sunday (kick-off times GMT):
Bologna (12) v AS Roma (6) 1330
Following their midweek UEFA Cup elimination by German club
Karlsruhe, Roma will be keen to get back on winning trail but
may find the Bologna attack of Russian Igor Kolyvanov and Swede
Kennet Andersson too big an obstacle.
Cagliari (17) v Perugia (5) 1330
Despite internecine strife, Perugia keep on winning and look
for fourth consecutive success against unsettled Cagliari.
Uruguayan striker Dario Silva of Cagliari and Perugia defender
Salvatore Matrecano are both out through suspension.
Juventus (1) v Napoli (9) 1330
In the 1980s this tie was the Platini v Maradona Show. On
Sunday it will be Croat Alen Boksic v Brazilian Beto, with
Juventus favoured to continue in the form shown in their 5-0
midweek European Champions' League rout of Austrians Rapid
Vienna.
Lazio (14) v Vicenza (3) 1330
Eliminated from the UEFA Cup in midweek by Spanish side
Tenerife and beaten in the league by Atalanta last Sunday, Lazio
could be headed for further trouble against in-form Vicenza.
Giuseppe Signori and Pierluigi Casiraghi lead the Lazio attack
while Uruguayan striker Marcelo Otero lines up for Vicenza.
AC Milan (4) v Atalanta (15) 1330
Their morale boosted by a 4-2 Champions' League win against
Sweden's IFK Gothenburg, champions Milan may be able to make
light of the absence of Yugoslav Dejan Savicevic, Tomas
Locatelli, Stefano Eranio and Franco Baresi. Roberto Baggio
returns to midfield behind strikers Marco Simone and Liberian
George Weah. Atalanta pose a threat in former Milan star Gigi
Lentini, a player with a point to prove.
Parma (11) v Fiorentina (7) 1930
Out-of-form Parma have not lost at home to Fiorentina in the
league since 1931. That record and possible Fiorentina
exhaustion following Thursday's Cup Winners' Cup qualification
with 1-1 draw away to Czech side Sparta Prague represent Parma's
best hopes.
Sampdoria (10) v Piacenza (8) 1330
All-Italian Piacenza come into this tie following wins
against Reggiana and Verona but are likely to find Sampdoria a
tougher task. Sampdoria field Roberto Mancini in attack, with
Frenchmen Christian Karembeu and Pierre Laigle and Argentine
Juan Veron in midfield. The Piacenza attack will be led by
Pasquale Luiso, scorer of six goals this season.
Udinese (13) v Reggiana (18) 1330
Reggiana, yet to win in seven league games, may be hard
pressed to open their winning account against an Udinese side
led by German striker Oliver Bierhoff but without defender
Giovanni Bia and midfielder Fabio Rossitto, both suspended.
Reggiana welcome back experienced Belgian defender George Grun.
Verona (16) v Internazionale (2) 1330
Inter struggled in their midweek UEFA Cup qualification,
defeating Austrian side Casino Graz only in a penalty shoot-out.
They may struggle against Verona too. Inter field a
full-strength multinational side while Verona look to the
experience of ex-Inter midfielder Pierluigi Orlandini and
ex-Sampdoria striker Filippo Maniero.
